name: JPverb
description: Algorithmic reverberator inspired by vintage Lexicon and Alesis units. Designed to produce long, lush, chorused reverberation tails — well-suited to synthetic sources rather than realistic spaces. Always outputs stereo.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Input signal (mono or stereo array)

inputs.name: t60
inputs.description: Approximate reverberation time in seconds (0.1..60). Time for the reverb to decay 60dB when damp == 0; does not affect early reflections.

inputs.name: damp
inputs.description: High-frequency damping as the reverb decays (0..1). 0 = no damping, 1 = very strong.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Scales size of internal delay-lines (0.5..5). Values below 1 can sound metallic.

inputs.name: earlyDiff
inputs.description: Shape of early reflections (0..1). >= 0.707 produces smooth exponential decay; lower values give a slower build-up of echoes.

inputs.name: modDepth
inputs.description: Depth of delay-line modulation (0..1). Combine with modFreq for chorusing.

inputs.name: modFreq
inputs.description: Frequency of delay-line modulation in Hz (0..10). Combine with modDepth for chorusing.

inputs.name: low
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the low band (0..1).

inputs.name: mid
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the mid band (0..1).

inputs.name: high
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the high band (0..1).

inputs.name: lowcut
inputs.description: Crossover frequency between the low and mid bands in Hz (100..6000).

inputs.name: highcut
inputs.description: Crossover frequency between the mid and high bands in Hz (1000..10000).

name: JPverbRaw
description: Raw multi-output form of the JPverb algorithmic reverberator. Prefer JPverb for the convenient single-input wrapper. Always outputs stereo.

inputs.name: in1
inputs.description: Left channel input.

inputs.name: in2
inputs.description: Right channel input.

inputs.name: damp
inputs.description: High-frequency damping as the reverb decays (0..1).

inputs.name: earlydiff
inputs.description: Shape of early reflections (0..1).

inputs.name: highband
inputs.description: Crossover frequency between mid and high bands in Hz (1000..10000).

inputs.name: highx
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the high band (0..1).

inputs.name: lowband
inputs.description: Crossover frequency between low and mid bands in Hz (100..6000).

inputs.name: lowx
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the low band (0..1).

inputs.name: mdepth
inputs.description: Depth of delay-line modulation in samples (0..50).

inputs.name: mfreq
inputs.description: Frequency of delay-line modulation in Hz (0..10).

inputs.name: midx
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the mid band (0..1).

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Scales size of internal delay-lines (0.5..5).

inputs.name: t60
inputs.description: Approximate reverberation time in seconds (0.1..60).

name: Greyhole
description: Complex echo-like effect inspired by the classic Eventide unit. A diffuser (similar to JPverb's) connected in a feedback loop with a long modulated delay-line — excels at spacey washes of sound. Always outputs stereo.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Input signal (mono or stereo array)

inputs.name: delayTime
inputs.description: Approximate delay time in seconds (0.1..60).

inputs.name: damp
inputs.description: High-frequency damping as the delay decays (0..1).

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Scales size of internal delay-lines (0.5..5). Values below 1 can sound metallic.

inputs.name: diff
inputs.description: Shape of the diffusion unit (0..1). Low values act as a delay-line; medium values build up slowly; >= 0.707 produces smooth exponential decay.

inputs.name: feedback
inputs.description: Amount of feedback through the system (0..1). 1.0 produces infinite sustain.

inputs.name: modDepth
inputs.description: Depth of delay-line modulation (0..1). Combine with modFreq for chorus and pitch variation.

inputs.name: modFreq
inputs.description: Frequency of delay-line modulation in Hz (0..10).

name: GreyholeRaw
description: Raw multi-output form of the Greyhole algorithmic delay. Prefer Greyhole for the convenient single-input wrapper. Always outputs stereo.

inputs.name: in1

inputs.name: in2

inputs.name: damping
inputs.description: High-frequency damping as the delay decays (0..1).

inputs.name: delaytime
inputs.description: Approximate delay time in seconds (0.1..60).

inputs.name: diffusion
inputs.description: Shape of the diffusion unit (0..1). >= 0.707 produces smooth exponential decay.

inputs.name: feedback
inputs.description: Feedback amount through the delay line (0..1).

inputs.name: moddepth
inputs.description: Depth of delay-line modulation in samples (0..50).

inputs.name: modfreq
inputs.description: Frequency of delay-line modulation in Hz (0..10).

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Scales size of internal delay-lines (0.5..5).

name: ComplexRes
description: Resonating filter that can be modulated at audio rate without blowing up. Implements the complex resonator structure from Parker & Bovermann (2013), 'Dynamic FM synthesis using a network of complex resonator filters'.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Input signal.

inputs.name: freq
inputs.description: Resonating frequency in Hz; can be modulated at audio rate.

inputs.name: decay
inputs.description: Decay time in seconds.

name: DiodeRingMod
description: Ring modulation based on the physical model of a diode.

inputs.name: car
inputs.description: Carrier signal.

inputs.name: mod
inputs.description: Modulator signal.

name: RMS
description: Root mean square of the input signal: sqrt(lpf1(x^2)) — first-order low-pass filtered squared input, then square-rooted, computed per sample.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Input signal.

inputs.name: lpFreq
inputs.description: Low-pass filter frequency in Hz.
